Supercilious

soo-per-SIL-ee-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Supercilious is showing arrogant or scornful superiority through one's expression or manner.

The gallery assistant's supercilious once-over made it clear she'd already decided the visitors in sneakers couldn't afford anything on the walls.

Worked Example

When the new intern asked a basic question, the senior analyst answered with a supercilious little laugh, as though the question itself were beneath him.

Supercilious is almost always apparent in the moment -- a raised eyebrow, a smirk, a dismissive glance -- rather than something you'd describe as a lifelong personality trait.

How Supercilious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

disdainful

disdainful: showing contempt or a lack of respect

snobbish

snobbish: believing oneself superior in taste or status

Antonyms

humble

humble: modest, not thinking oneself superior

respectful

respectful: showing genuine regard for others

How Strong Is It? — smug → supercilious → contemptuous

smug vs. supercilious

smug vs. supercilious: Smug is self-satisfied but doesn't necessarily involve looking down on other people the way supercilious does.

contemptuous vs. supercilious

contemptuous vs. supercilious: Contemptuous goes further than supercilious, showing open scorn rather than just a superior glance.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — super-

prefix — super-: above, over (Latin super)

root — -cilious

root — -cilious: eyebrow (Latin cilium)

Put it together

Put it together: Supercilious comes from Latin super- ('above') plus cilium ('eyebrow') -- literally 'with the eyebrow raised above.' Picture someone lifting one eyebrow to look down on you: that's exactly the scornful, superior expression supercilious describes.

Use the root in a new word: cilia

Use the root in a new word: cilia: In biology, cilia are the tiny hair-like structures that line certain cells -- from the same Latin cilium ('eyelash/eyebrow') at the heart of supercilious, though cilium itself rarely shows up in everyday English words.

Root Check

Word Choice

Supercilious usually describes a specific look or tone in a specific moment -- the raised eyebrow, the dismissive glance -- rather than a person's whole personality (that's closer to haughty, a word you'll also meet in this unit).
